item.text: Tracing an ordinary object like a button reveals how broad social changes enter daily life. Its materials can reflect trade routes, industrialization, or environmental pressures; its manufacture can expose technologies and labor conditions; and its styles can signal class, gender, military rank, or cultural identity. Changes from handmade bone or shell buttons to mass-produced plastic ones, for example, connect personal clothing to factories, global commerce, and consumer culture. A small object thus makes large historical forces tangible and relatable.
